claims.statement: src/proxy.ts (the Next.js 16 replacement for middleware.ts) runs on every matched request except static assets/_next/HMR, calls updateSession() to rotate Supabase auth cookies, and deliberately does not redirect unauthenticated users.

(app)/layout.tsx is the real access-control gate: it builds a Supabase client, calls auth.getClaims(), and redirects to /login when claims are missing; Server Actions independently re-check auth via their own requireUser()-style helper rather than relying on the layout.

createClient(), getCatalogMap(), and getCurrentBodyweight() are each wrapped in React cache(), so within one request layout, page, and Server Action call sites that pass the same client instance share one query per underlying table instead of one per call site.

React cache() memoizes by argument identity, so the shared request-memoized Supabase client from createClient() is what lets getCatalogMap and getCurrentBodyweight dedupe across callers in the same request. A fresh client at each call site would miss the cache, and a different user id is a separate entry.

The weekly Coach API (GET /api/coach/v1/weekly) is the sole elevated read path: it has no browser session, so it uses a separate server-held secret client that bypasses RLS, and every query on that path carries an explicit COACH_API_USER_ID predicate. The route is capability-token gated, read-only, and no-store/noindex.

The four tabs are Lift (/), Track (/analytics and /analytics/*, plus /history/*), Program (/program and /program/*), and You (/settings and /settings/*), each matched by its own predicate in app-shell.tsx.

logSet() re-authenticates via requireUser(), inserts into set_log using an idempotency_key so a unique-constraint conflict (23505) returns the existing row instead of erroring, computes e1rm at write time, then calls recomputeAndUpsertStat() to rebuild user_exercise_stat; if that rebuild throws, the function still returns the successful set write with a recomputeWarning instead of failing the write.

Mutation Server Actions call revalidatePath() for every route their write could affect immediately after the write/cache-rebuild completes, e.g. logSet revalidates the session route, its recap route, and the per-exercise history route, while other actions in the same file revalidate /, /analytics, /analytics/month, /analytics/volume, /analytics/coach, and /program as appropriate.

user_exercise_stat is a derived, rebuildable cache of each exercise's current e1RM and personal coefficient, rebuilt from set_log via recomputeStat() after relevant writes. It is never the source of truth for PR eligibility, which replays saved set_log rows through workoutRecords().

Server Component pages batch their independent queries with Promise.all rather than issuing them sequentially; for example the Home page resolves the next workout, last finished session, and week-record chips concurrently, then a second Promise.all for the last-session summary, week records, and the full set_log scan.

The app is organized in three layers: a framework-free strength engine (src/lib/strength/) with no Next.js or Supabase imports, server loaders and Server Actions that are the only application code talking to Postgres, and an App Router UI where Server Components render hydrated data and a small set of Client Components handle interaction.

AppShell still exposes exactly four tabs (Lift, Track, Program, You) and also mounts AgentEntry whenever chrome is visible except on /coach. hideAppChrome hides the tab bar and the agent entry on /session/, /workout/next, /program/new, and /program/?mode=edit. isTrackPath keeps Track active on /history/.

Auth is split across three places: src/proxy.ts only calls updateSession() to rotate Supabase cookies and does not redirect, (app)/layout.tsx is the page gate via auth.getClaims() redirecting to /login, and Server Actions independently re-check getClaims() through requireUser() because a layout guard does not protect a directly invoked action.

The app keeps no parallel analytics schema or materialized views. set_log is the sole authoritative ledger, and Track summaries, Coach, month review, and PR pills are TypeScript functions computed over that ledger at read time, with windows such as 21 Chicago days, the last 8 session-bests, and the seven-day Coach report applied in the loader or a pure helper.

sessionTarget() is computed client-side in a useMemo against server-hydrated stats and history so swap, rep, and RIR edits update with no network round trip, while Track, Coach, and month-review aggregation over history runs server-side and ships already-shaped data to client chart components.

The rest timer starts immediately on local set logging and lives in RestTimerProvider on session/[id]/layout.tsx, persisting its end timestamp outside the revalidated page so a set_log refresh cannot reset it. A failed write surfaces a visible card error and reverts the optimistic row, and PR pills come only from persisted set_log rows via loadWorkoutRecords and workoutRecords.

Every user-owned table is scoped by row-level security to auth.uid(), with profile using id. The weekly Coach API is the sole elevated-privilege read exception, and it still enforces one explicit user predicate on every query rather than relying on the bypassed RLS.

The shipped in-app agent chat is a separate cookie-auth, user-scoped path from the weekly Coach secret client. GET and POST /api/agent/chat use getClaims() and the public server client, Slice 0 binds only the four read tools, and the UI is AgentEntry plus the full-screen /coach page rather than an unbuilt design.
